newsitem.title: USA: Simpson emphatically denies killing ex-wife and friend.
newsitem.headline: Simpson emphatically denies killing ex-wife and friend.

text.p: Testifying in court for the first time, O.J. Simpson proclaimed his innocence on Friday in the most emphatic terms so far, saying he "absolutely" did not murder his ex-wife and her friend.

In a dramatic exchange that concluded Simpson's 4-1/2-hour stint on the witness stand in his civil trial, Daniel Petrocelli, the plaintiffs' lead attorney, lashed into the former football star with a series of harsh accusations.
"You had gloves, you had a hat, you had a knife. And you used that Bronco to go to Nicole's condo, didn't you?" Petrocelli asked in a calm voice.
"That's absolutely not true," Simpson said firmly, looking directly at the jury.
"And you confronted Nicole Brown Simpson and you killed her, didn't you?" Petrocelli asked.
"That is absolutely not true," Simpson replied forcefully.
"And you killed Ronald Goldman, did you or did you not?" Petrocelli asked.
"That's absolutely not true," Simpson shot back.

Glaring at Simpson from the lectern, Petrocelli then accused him of driving from the murder scene outside his ex- wife's Brentwood townhouse to his mansion two miles (3 km) away. "You got onto your property and you bumped into a wall at 10:50 - 10:51 (p.m.)," Petrocelli asserted.
"That's absolutely not true," Simpson said.
"You dropped one of the gloves there and you put your clothing in a bag and you put it behind (a car in the driveway)," the attorney stated.
"That's absolutely not true," Simpson repeated.

Petrocelli then claimed that Simpson bled on an outside air conditioner in a narrow walkway where the bloody glove was found and on the driveway of his estate. But Simpson continued his litany of denials, saying, "That is absolutely incorrect."
During the entire tense exchange, jurors listened with rapt attention, sometimes scribbling furiously in their notebooks.

Simpson was acquitted in October of last year of double murder charges, but he now faces a wrongful-death civil lawsuit brought by the victims' families. He is due to return to the witness stand on Monday and may continue testifying on Tuesday as well.

Simpson began his first full day of testimony denying that he had ever beaten Nicole Brown Simpson but claiming that she struck him "numerous times." In a sometimes blistering interrogation, Petrocelli confronted him with the domestic violence allegations that have haunted him since his criminal trial.

While jurors looked at photos of a bruised, battered Nicole Brown Simpson projected on a giant courtroom TV screen, Simpson denied abusing his ex-wife and said she lied when she wrote in her journals and told others that he had beaten her.

Instead, directly contradicting the testimony of witnesses in both trials, Simpson portrayed himself as the victim of an erratic and sometimes violent woman. He said that even after their 1992 divorce, she was the one who pursued him.

It was the first courtroom confrontation between Simpson and opposing attorneys representing the families of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman, who have brought a civil case seeking to find him responsbile -- and financially "liable" -- for the murders.

Testifying as a "hostile" witness, Simpson started off speaking calmly. But as the questioning turned combative, he at times became exasperated, sighing heavily and clenching his fists in front of him.
Goldman's father, Fred, and sister, Kim, glared at Simpson from the spectators' galleries. Jurors leaned forward in their seats to catch every word.
Attorneys for the families have contended that Simpson abused, stalked and threatened his ex-wife, finally killing her in June 1994 when he could no longer control her.

While Simpson chose not to testify at his criminal trial, the rules of civil procedure required him to either take the witness stand or forfeit the case, which could have cost him millions of dollars in damages.
